_source: Guardian nameplate copy reproduced VERBATIM from ~/src/website/public/wolves/characters/characters.json (authoritative), cross-checked against the overlay strings in ~/src/website/src/data/wolves-intro-sequence.ts. The two RECAST plates are the exception and are marked as such: the owner replaced Bob Killen with Cortney Nickerson and Laura Santamaria with Orlin, and neither has an authored identity, so those plates carry the owner's own name string and nothing else. A name that is missing is omitted; a name is never invented.
_timeline: Windows come from wolves-intro-sequence.ts, which records them as frame-verified against the real embed. They are keyed to the SOURCE absolute timeline; every `at` below is that value minus the verified startOffset of 2.0s, so it lands on the trimmed segment.

The two recasts changed WHO is credited, never WHICH shot: the windows are untouched, so nothing here needs re-verifying against the frames.

Shares Cortney's window and her `group`, which is what the site's row is: her plate on the left, the bond on the right.

plates.name: Karl
plates.note: Kat Cosgrove's documented bond. Name and species reproduced from wolves-guardian-dinosaur-bonds.ts + wolves-dinosaur-species.ts; nothing here is composed.

THE TITLE COVER -- the owner's name for it. Owner instruction: 'replace the dino/QR sequence with wolves.jpg, the same comic at the end of europa'. It takes the whole window the 23-shot comic/QR cycle held (22.5 - 36.0), and it is the SAME asset the Europa director's cut ends on (~/Videos/wolves-directors-cut/STORYBOARD.md, 'Scene: Comic cover'). What left with the cycle: the MakeMeAComic QR panel and the Amber Graner quote, both owner-authored -- flagged in issue #90 so dropping them is a decision rather than a side effect.

WHY THE COVER IDENTITIES ARE CAPTIONS AND NOT PLATES: the art is square (9075x9075) and the frame is 16:9, so it fills the middle 1080px and leaves 420px of margin either side. A Guardian plate is 561px wide (tools/plate.py), so the owner's three authored cover identities could not be plates without covering the ink -- which the owner ruled out ('can't have the nameplates cover the art'). Every authored string is carried verbatim in the caption boxes below; only the chrome changed, to the white/chamfered/blue-hairline box the owner picked ('no tilt, use the same tech outline on the box but keep them white'). The two framing lines are owner-authored too.

The margins show a RANDOM Bluefin wallpaper per render, by owner request; cards/render-cards.mjs records which one it rolled in wallpapers.json beside the PNG, so a frame stays reproducible.

Still open, all in issue #90: 'Wielder of the Kube' is the owner's spelling here and 'Weilder of the Arcane' is theirs on Cortney's plate -- both reproduced, neither corrected. The owner wrote 'DEINONYCHUS // speciesname'; ANTIRRHOPUS is PROPOSED from the art_label 'Deinonychus antirrhopus' the deleted comic entries carried, not decided. The trailing space in 'Really Hungry ' is authored and kept. The second Blueberry caption has NO NAME ROW: the owner wrote a class and a title for 'little girl behind him' and withheld her name in the plate request, then wrote 'Introducing Rafael and Lakshmi' as the framing line. Naming the child on her own caption is a claim the owner has not made in that place, so the row stays out.

plates.name: Alamo
plates.note: Natali Vlatko's documented bond. Takes the christoph-natali group rather than a new one: three cards are visible together in this shot and that row is exactly what the group exemption is for. Natali's own plate is `raised` (top 28%) and the bond sits at the row's bottom right, so they do not stack -- the same separation the site gets from `position: fixed; right: 5%; bottom: 10%`. ART CAPPED at 200px, and this is a FRAME JUDGEMENT, not a proportion: at full height Alamo's artwork rose to y=379 and covered 'Natali Vlatko' and 'Shipwright of Kubernetes' on her raised plate -- verified on the burned frame at t=90, not in the manifest. Capped, the card's top sits at 640 against her plate's bottom at 611. The site has no such cap because nothing there is 1920x1080 with a raised plate above the bond; here a legible credit outranks the artwork's scale.
